page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-16 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core performance, scoring in the top quartile for stress-ng CPU tasks and showing high execution rates in text processing and small-model language generation. Multi-core performance across Geekbench, PassMark, and compression tests consistently measures in the middle tier. A hardware tradeoff appears in the memory subsystem: while cached 16 KB read throughput exceeds 1130 GB/s, uncached large-block operations register lower bandwidth, falling to 38.53 GB/s for read transfers and 12.89 GB/s for write transfers.

The 1:2 resource allocation offers cost efficiency for compute-centric pipelines where high memory capacity is unnecessary. Performance metrics for static web serving, Clang compilation, and Redis operations show steady throughput. The instance profile is suited for build and compilation servers, continuous integration tasks, batch processing, and lightweight inference workloads that are not bottlenecked by uncached memory write bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-16 is a virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, offering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores and 32 GB of system memory. Its hardware profile yields a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache and advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or physical GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, it displays strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core metrics and solid text processing throughput. Uncached memory write bandwidth presents a notable performance bottleneck. Because hardware resources favor raw processing capacity over high memory density, this instance delivers efficient resource allocation for compute-bound tasks. It is best applied to workloads such as software compilation, batch processing, containerized microservices, static web hosting, and small-model inference tasks that do not depend on high uncached memory write rates.
